ingredients.item: egg yolk (from a large egg (~50 - 55g / 2 oz), fridge cold is fine)
ingredients.name: egg yolk (from a large egg (~50 - 55g / 2 oz), fridge cold is fine)

ingredients.item: lemon juice (or white wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar, plus more as desired)
ingredients.name: lemon juice (or white wine vinegar or apple cider vinegar, plus more as desired)

ingredients.item: Dijon mustard ((substitute yellow mustard, not hot English mustard))
ingredients.name: Dijon mustard ((substitute yellow mustard, not hot English mustard))

ingredients.item: heaped cooking salt / kosher salt
ingredients.name: heaped cooking salt / kosher salt

ingredients.item: Pinch white pepper ((substitute black pepper - but they will be visible))
ingredients.name: Pinch white pepper ((substitute black pepper - but they will be visible))

ingredients.item: grapeseed oil or other plain flavoured oil (, or up to 50% extra virgin olive oil (Note 1))
ingredients.name: grapeseed oil or other plain flavoured oil (, or up to 50% extra virgin olive oil (Note 1))

instructions: Mix yolk - Use a small to medium bowl. If it's too big, the mixture will be too thinly spread at the start for the yolk and oil to catch on the beater. Place everything except the oil in a bowl. Give it a quick beat with an electric beater to combine the ingredients.

Slow pour and constant beating - With the electric beater running on medium-high (speed 8 of 10), start pouring in the oil in a thin, steady stream. Aim for the beaters so it's mixed in straight away and move the beater around the bowl as needed to beat the oil in. Continue with the remaining oil in the same thin stream, pausing the pour whenever needed to give the mayonnaise a chance to catch up and absorb the oil before adding more.

Finish by hand - Stop beating once all the oil is added and beaten in, do not keep beating unnecessarily (it can make it split). Use a rubber spatula to scoop around the bowl to catch any residual oil splatters and mix it in.

Voila! Homemade mayonnaise! It should be the consistency of softened butter. Use as you do shop-bought mayonnaise, though it's so beautiful you could even just spread it on warm bread like butter (Try it. It's amazing!)

Follow the same steps as the electric beater but use a hand whisk instead. While constantly whisking, pour the oil in a thin steady stream onto the spot where the whisk is moving. Set your bowl on a damp tea towel to stop it from moving.

ingredients.name: Lemon wedges

instructions: Pre-heat oven to 190°C / 375°F (170°C fan). Sauté potatoes for 4 min, then add remaining vegetables, salt, pepper and toss briefly. Divide vegetables between parcels, top with seasoned fish, dill, oil and wine. Seal the parcels and bake 18 min, then rest 3 min before opening.
Preheat oven to 190°C / 375°F (170°C fan-forced).

Cook potato - Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the potatoes and cook for 4 minutes, stirring regularly (use 2 wooden spoons if needed). They should pick up a little colour but not too much.
Cook the rest of vegetables - Add the zucchini, capsicum, red onion, garlic and half of the salt and pepper. Toss everything together for about 1 minute, then set aside.

Place two pieces of foil on your work surface (50cm / 20" long x 30cm / 12" wide), then top with a sheet of baking paper/parchment paper (40cm / 16" x 30cm / 12"). Divide the vegetables between the two, placing them in the middle. (Note 4)
Fish - Pat the snapper fillets dry, season both side with the remaining salt and pepper, then place on top of the vegetables.
Place 3 dill sprigs on top of each fish. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and pour 1 tbsp of white wine over each.

Build the parcels (video is helpful here) - Bring the short edges of the foil and baking paper together and fold over twice to seal that side. Press down gently along the fold to flatten it. Then, working on one end, fold each corner in to form a triangle, then fold that triangle over twice more to lock in the seal. Repeat on the other end so both ends are sealed the same way. Redo the same with the other parcel.
Bake & rest - Place the parcels on a baking tray and cook for 18 minutes. Remove and let rest for 3 minutes. (Once cooked, the core fish temperature should read at least 55°C / 130°F.)
Serving - Grand opening time! Open the parcels, watch the steam escape, squeeze some lemon juice over and eat while hot with some crusty bread on the side.

instructions: Whisk wet and dry in separate bowls, combine, stir in cheese and grated zucchini (excess water squeezed out). Bake 25 min in flour dusted or paper lined muffin tin (cheese gets stuck!) at 200°C/390°F (180°C fan).
Preheat oven to 200°C/390°F (180°C fan-forced).

Prepare muffin tin - Spray a 12 hole standard muffin tin generously with oil. If your non-stick coating isn't in great shape (like mine), either use liners instead or lightly dust with flour - I prefer this, for golden muffin sides and base. (Note 3 for how to flour dust pans). Cheese is a strong glue!!
Grate the zucchini with a standard box grater. Grab handfuls and squeeze out excess water (no need to go to extremes with a tea towel).
Dry ingredients - Whisk Dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Wet ingredients - Whisk Wet ingredients in a separate bowl.
Combine wet and dry - Pour Wet into the Dry ingredients bowl. Mix 8 times or until flour is almost mixed in but you can still see some.
Add zucchini and cheese then mix as few times as possible just to incorporate remaining bits of flour - no more than 7 big stirs (secret to soft muffs).
The batter will be quite thick - don't worry, the zucchini releases moisture as it bakes.

Bake 25 min - Divide between 12 holes in muffin in (I use an ice cream scooper). Bake for 25 minutes or until the muffins are golden and crusty, and a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.

Cool for 10 minutes, then transfer to cooling rack. If they are a bit stuck (cheese!), run a knife around the rim then invert and bang the pan on the counter so they tumble out. Serve warm for optimum experience!
